description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/filenode.rs:860-874 (handle_filenode_copy account-existence checks).

```rust
if !backend.account_exists(caller, &from_account_id).await? {
    return Err(JmapError::account_not_found());
}
if !backend.account_exists(caller, &account_id).await? {
    return Err(JmapError::account_not_found());
}
```

Both checks return the same generic `accountNotFound` error type.
RFC 8620 §5.4 defines TWO distinct error types for a `Foo/copy` call:

> "fromAccountNotFound": The "fromAccountId" does not correspond to a
> valid account.
> "fromAccountNotSupportedByMethod": The "fromAccountId" given
> corresponds to a valid account, but the account does not support
> this data type.
> "accountNotFound" (inherited from §3.6.2): The accountId does not
> correspond to a valid account.

A client receiving `accountNotFound` cannot tell whether their
source or destination account is the problem. For `fromAccountId`
the error type should be `fromAccountNotFound`, not
`accountNotFound`. For account-exists-but-unsupported, the error
type should be `fromAccountNotSupportedByMethod` — but there is no
support-check path because `supports_type` is unused by this crate
(see bd:JMAP-510h.34 / .43).

Concrete impact:

- A monitoring/logging stack that classifies JMAP errors by type sees
  source-account misconfiguration as "account does not exist", with
  no way to distinguish "the source they gave us is bogus" from "the
  destination they're trying to write to is bogus". Operators get
  paged for the wrong thing.
- A client UX layer that renders different messages for "your source
  is bad" vs "your destination is bad" cannot do so based on the
  error type — it must parse the surrounding response context.

Required fix:

1. Replace `JmapError::account_not_found()` for the from-side check
   with a new `JmapError::from_account_not_found()` (define on
   jmap_types::JmapError per RFC 8620 §5.4 error table). This is a
   foundation change at the canonical jmap-types crate, propagated
   through every Foo/copy handler across the workspace.
2. Wire `supports_type::<FileNode>()` on the from-side (separately
   from the unconditional registration covered by .43) so a backend
   that opts out of the type can return
   `fromAccountNotSupportedByMethod` rather than ambiguous
   `accountNotFound`.

Propagation: this is a foundation-level issue. jmap-mail-server's
EmailSubmission/copy and any future Foo/copy handler will hit the
same gap. Fix the foundation first per the workspace canonical-
template propagation rule.

LABELS: api-contract, leakage, spec
title: handle_filenode_copy returns 'accountNotFound' for both fromAccountId and accountId; RFC 8620 §5.4 defines distinct error types
